title: What Kind of Lover Are You?

chapters.title: How you fall
chapters.teaser: Fast, slow, sideways or all at once. The way your soul actually falls for someone.

chapters.title: Your flirting style
chapters.teaser: What you think you're doing, what they think you're doing, and the one move that lands.

chapters.title: Your attachment pattern
chapters.teaser: Clingy, cool, steady or somewhere in between. How you hold on when you care.

chapters.title: Jealousy and your trigger
chapters.teaser: The exact thing that sets you off, and what you do instead of saying it.

chapters.title: Yeon's red flag report
chapters.teaser: The love habit you keep repeating. Yeon does not soften this chapter.

chapters.title: What you actually need
chapters.teaser: Not your type. Your match. The kind of person and love that lets you relax.

chapters.how-you-fall: You don't fall, you decide. Somewhere around the third conversation you look at a person and think, yes, this one is worth building something with, and from then on you are all in. Gap is the tall tree, and trees don't wander off to see what else is growing. The catch is that your decision often comes before the other person has made theirs. You can mistake your own certainty for proof that it's mutual. You also fall for potential. You see who someone could become in five years and you love that version a little too early. When it works, it's beautiful: steady, loyal, protective love that makes people feel chosen. When it doesn't, you stay far longer than the evidence allows, because leaving feels like admitting you planted in the wrong field.
chapters.flirting: Your flirting looks a lot like mentoring. You ask about their plans, you give advice nobody requested, you show up with a solution to the problem they mentioned last Tuesday. To you, this is romance. To them, it can feel like a very attractive performance review. You are not a giggler or a hair-twirler. You flirt with competence and reliability, and the people who get it find it irresistible. The people who don't think you're just being nice. Try this: say one thing you like about them that has nothing to do with their potential. Not "you'd be great at this job." Something like "I like how you laugh at your own jokes before the punchline." Small, specific, a little soft. It lands harder than any plan you could make for them.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gap, you love like a promise. Steady, loyal, the person everyone wishes they'd dated first.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Also the person who turns a second date into a five-year development plan.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: That's devotion! Love the person in front of you, Gap, not the five-year plan.

chapters.how-you-fall: You fall sideways. Eul is the vine and the wildflower, and vines don't charge at things, they wind. One day you're just friends, the next you've memorized their coffee order, their sister's name and the exact playlist that fixes their bad days, and you realize you've been falling for weeks. You attach through closeness and small daily contact. Texting good morning, sharing memes, borrowing their hoodie. It's gentle and it's sneaky, even to you. The beauty of this is that your love feels natural and easy, never forced. The risk is that you can wrap yourself around a person before you've checked whether they're a strong trellis or a wobbly fence post. You adapt to fit them so well that it's hard to tell, later, which parts of you were yours.
chapters.flirting: You are a natural. Flirting is basically your second language, and most of the time you don't even know you're doing it. The tilted head, the "wait, tell me more," the way you remember a detail they mentioned once and bring it up three days later. People feel seen around you, and that's the whole trick. You also flirt in groups beautifully, drawing the quiet one into the conversation so they think you're the warmest person alive. The downside: people sometimes can't tell if you're into them or just being you. If you actually like someone, make it unmistakable once. Ask them to something with just the two of you, and name it. "I'd like to take you to that ramen place. Like a date." Vines are allowed to be direct.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Eul, you love like a vine. Gentle, close, woven into every little part of their day.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: And by month three you've adopted their music taste, their friends and their opinions on cilantro.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You're just so adaptable! People feel completely seen by you.

chapters.how-you-fall: You fall fast and in public. Byeong is the sun, and the sun has never once been subtle. When you like someone, everyone knows by Friday, including your group chat, your mom and possibly the barista. You fall for energy: someone who laughs at your jokes, who matches your enthusiasm, who makes ordinary nights feel like an event. The first weeks with you are a highlight reel. Spontaneous plans, big gestures, you making them feel like the most interesting person in any room. The tricky part comes when the shine settles into routine. You love loving, and you can mistake a quiet phase for a dying flame. It usually isn't. Real warmth doesn't need to be at full brightness all the time. Even the sun has evenings.
chapters.flirting: Your flirting is generous and slightly overwhelming, in a fun way. You compliment loudly, you tease, you make the plan, you pay for the snacks, you invite them to the thing with your twelve friends. You flirt like you're hosting. People feel instantly welcome, which is why you're so easy to crush on. The flip side is that your warmth is the same for everyone, so the person you actually like may not realize they're special. They watched you light up the whole table. Here's the move: give them something you don't give the room. Quiet attention. Lower your voice, ask a real question, and stay on their answer for longer than feels natural. Your spotlight is lovely. Your undivided focus is unforgettable.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Byeong, you love like sunshine. Big, warm, generous. Everyone feels invited.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Exactly. Everyone. Including the person you're not dating. They're confused.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You're just naturally warm! Your first dates are legendary.

chapters.how-you-fall: You fall slowly and then completely. Jeong is the candle, and candles don't light up a stadium, they light up a face across a small table. You need a real conversation, the kind that goes past midnight and somehow turns into talking about your childhood, before anything in you moves. Once it does, you feel it intensely. You remember everything: the song playing when they first held your hand, the exact phrasing of their text. Your love is intimate, observant and deeply personal. People who are loved by you feel understood in a way they rarely have before. The risk is that you can fall for the inner world you've imagined in someone, filling silences with meaning they didn't intend. Check in with the real person, not just the beautiful version in your head.
chapters.flirting: Your flirting is quiet and devastating. You don't make a show. You listen, you notice, and then you say something so specific that the other person feels like you've read their diary. "You go quiet when people talk about your dad." A little risky, very effective. You flirt through attention and meaning: a song you send at 11pm, a book you think they'd like, a thoughtful question nobody else asked. With people you're not into, you're warm but polite. With someone you like, the warmth gets focused like a flame. The challenge is that it can be so subtle they miss it entirely. Add one obvious signal. Hold eye contact a second longer. Say "I like talking to you." Candles are allowed to flicker on purpose.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Jeong, you love like candlelight. Close, warm, and so attentive it feels like being read.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: And you remember every single thing they did wrong. With dates.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: That's just how deeply you care! You notice everything.

chapters.how-you-fall: Your way of falling is like a mountain moves: very slowly, and then it's permanent. Mu is the big hill, the boulder, the thing you can lean against without checking. You don't do impulsive crushes. You observe someone for a long time, quietly gathering evidence that they're trustworthy, consistent and worth the effort of letting in. By the time you show interest, you've basically already decided. That means rejection hits harder than you'd ever show. On the bright side, when you choose someone, they feel deeply safe. You become their shelter: the person who drives over in the rain, fixes the shelf, remembers the doctor appointment. The risk is that you're so focused on being solid that your partner might not realize you're also falling, because mountains don't exactly blush.
chapters.flirting: You flirt by being useful, and you may not even call it flirting. Carrying their bags, making sure they got home, showing up with snacks because they mentioned they skipped lunch. It's steady, practical care, and the people who notice it melt. The people who don't might wonder if you're interested at all, because you rarely say the soft thing out loud. Your humor helps a lot here. Dry, understated jokes are your secret weapon, and when you let them out, people get a glimpse of the warm landscape behind the cliff face. Try one small step past comfort: tell them you like them, plainly. You don't need poetry. "I like spending time with you" from a mountain sounds like a whole sonnet.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Mu, you love like a mountain. Solid, protective, the safest place anyone's ever stood.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Also about as emotionally chatty as a mountain.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Your love is in actions! You drive over in the rain.

chapters.how-you-fall: You fall by tending. Gi is the garden soil, the field that feeds everything planted in it. You notice what someone needs before they do: the snack, the charger, the reassurance after a bad day at work. Caring for them is how you realize you like them, often after you've already been doing it for weeks. Your love is warm, attentive and incredibly practical. Partners feel looked after in a way that's rare. The danger is that you can confuse being needed with being loved. You might fall for people who need a lot of tending, because being useful feels safe, and slowly end up doing the emotional housework for two. Ask yourself early: if I stopped helping, would they still want me here? With the right person, the answer is an obvious yes.
chapters.flirting: You flirt like a really good host. You check if they're comfortable, you remember they don't like spicy food, you send them the article about the thing they mentioned. People feel calm and cared for around you, and that quiet warmth is extremely attractive. You're also funnier than people expect, with an earthy, self-deprecating humor that sneaks up on them. What you don't do is make the first obvious move. You'd rather create the perfect conditions and wait for them to step in, like planting seeds and hoping for rain. Sometimes it works. Sometimes the other person thinks you're just nice to everyone. Try being the rain once. Send the text that says "I'd like to see you again, just us." The garden will forgive you for being bold.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gi, you love like a garden. Patient, nurturing, everyone around you just grows.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: You also love like an unpaid personal assistant. With overtime.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You're so caring! People feel completely at home with you.

chapters.how-you-fall: Your way of falling is like a sword is drawn: decisively and with commitment. Gyeong is raw metal, the axe, the blade that has to be forged. You don't do vague. You know pretty quickly if you're interested, and once you are, you pursue with clarity. No games, no hints, just "I like you, let's go to dinner." This directness is refreshing and a little intimidating. You fall for strength, honesty and people who don't fold the first time you push back. Respect comes first. Without it, attraction dies fast. When you love, you love loyally and protectively, the kind of partner who would fight the world for their person. The catch is that you can treat love a bit like a mission, and a mission sometimes forgets to stop and enjoy the view.
chapters.flirting: You flirt by challenging. You tease, debate, poke holes in their opinions and see if they push back. If they do, you're delighted. If they shrink, you lose interest. It's an unusual style, and with the right person it creates incredible sparks. With the wrong one it can feel like being cross-examined. You're also extremely honest, so compliments from you are rare and therefore powerful. When you say "you look good," people believe it. Your growth area is softness. Let yourself be playful without winning, or admit you're nervous. "I'm actually a bit nervous right now" from someone as confident as you is incredibly disarming. The blade is impressive. The hand that holds it gently is what people fall for.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gyeong, you love like a sword. Loyal, protective, you'd fight the whole world for your person.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: You'd also fight your person. About how they load the dishwasher.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You're just honest! Your compliments actually mean something.

chapters.how-you-fall: You fall for the details. Sin is the jewel, the polished silver ring, metal that has already been refined into something beautiful. You notice how someone dresses, how they speak to waiters, whether they text in full sentences. Taste matters to you more than you'd admit. When someone passes your many quiet tests, you fall gracefully and with real tenderness. You make love feel elegant and special, like being invited into a beautiful room. Underneath the polish, though, you're sensitive. A careless comment can stay with you for weeks, and you might pull back before you're hurt, just in case. You also fall for an idea of perfection sometimes, and real people, with their messy kitchens and odd habits, can never quite match it. Let them be imperfect. So are you.
chapters.flirting: The way you flirt is refined and slightly mysterious. A well-timed compliment, a glance, a perfectly chosen gift that shows you noticed exactly what they like. You're elegant without trying, and people often feel slightly nervous around you because you seem so put together. You also flirt through banter: witty, a little cutting, always clever. The issue is that you can be so polished that people can't tell if you like them or if this is simply your default charm. And you hate rejection so much that you rarely risk being clear. Try letting one crack show. A slightly embarrassing story, a real laugh, a direct "I've been hoping you'd text." The jewel shines brighter when it catches light, and light gets in through the cracks.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Sin, you love like a jewel. Elegant, thoughtful, everything you touch feels special.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: And you judged their font choice in the group chat. Don't lie.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You have beautiful taste! People feel honored to be chosen by you.

chapters.how-you-fall: You fall like a wave: big, sudden and with a pull that surprises everyone, including you. Im is the ocean, the great river, water that moves and refuses to stay still. You're drawn to people who make life feel bigger, the ones who talk about moving to Lisbon on a whim or who can keep up with your curiosity at 2am. You fall through adventure and ideas. A great conversation is your favorite kind of date. The first phase with you is thrilling: spontaneous trips, deep talks, the feeling of being swept up. The trouble comes when the tide turns into routine. You love freedom, and any whiff of being contained can make you drift. That's not because you don't care. It's because oceans need room. Find someone who swims, not someone who builds a pool.
chapters.flirting: The way you flirt is effortless and a little hypnotic. You're curious, you ask interesting questions, and you make people feel like the most fascinating person you've met all month. You're great at playful mystery: answering a question with a question, leaving at the right moment, texting something intriguing then going quiet. It's magnetic, and you know it. The risk is that people can't tell if you're serious or just enjoying the current. Also, you might flirt with three people at once, not out of malice but because you genuinely find everyone interesting. If you like someone for real, slow the wave down. Make a plan and keep it. Show up on time. For a person who's used to you drifting, reliability is the most romantic thing you can offer.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Im, you love like the ocean. Big, adventurous, people feel swept away by you.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: And then the tide goes out and they're standing alone on the beach.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You just need freedom! You never try to change anyone.

chapters.how-you-fall: You fall like mist settles: quietly, gradually, and then everything is soft and changed. Gye is the rain, the dew, the gentle water that soaks into everything. You don't fall for loud people. You fall for someone who feels like a secret, someone whose inner world seems as layered as yours. Often you fall in your imagination first, writing whole stories about a person before you've had a proper conversation. Your love is romantic, intuitive and deeply emotional. You sense what your partner feels before they say it. The danger is that your imagination can be more beautiful than reality, and you might stay loyal to a dream long after the actual person stopped showing up for it. Love the real one, too, not just the one in your head.
chapters.flirting: As a flirt, you're subtle, dreamy and a bit hard to catch. A shy smile, a song recommendation that says everything you won't, a meaningful look across the room. You're excellent at making people feel deeply understood, because you really do pick up on their moods. You often flirt through creativity: a drawing, a playlist, a poem in the notes app you might never send. The trouble is that many people miss your signals completely, and you'd rather vanish than risk being too obvious. Here's a gentle challenge. Send the thing. The playlist, the text, the "I've been thinking about you." Rain doesn't apologize for falling. And the people worth having are usually waiting for exactly that kind of quiet courage.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gye, you love like soft rain. Gentle, romantic, you feel everything they feel.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: You also wrote a whole love story about someone you've spoken to twice.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You're just so intuitive! Your playlists are love letters.
